instruction: Configure Chrome to send 'Do Not Track' requests with my browsing traffic to protect my privacy.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":false,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling Do Not Track in Chrome privacy settings. Verified that the getter reads from enable_do_not_track field in Preferences.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads 'enable_do_not_track' field from Chrome Preferences file - this is the standard Chrome field for DNT setting
Metric 'exact_match' appropriately compares the extracted value against expected 'true' string
Postconfig restarts Chrome to ensure preferences are persisted and readable, avoiding stale state issues
Complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (enable DNT) and evaluator verifies exactly that requirement
Cross-platform support: getter handles Windows, macOS, and Linux with correct preference file paths
Error handling present: getter returns 'false' on errors, which is reasonable default behavior
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter returns string 'true'/'false' instead of boolean true/false. While this works correctly with exact_match and the expected value, using boolean types would be more conventional. This is a very minor stylistic issue that doesn't affect correctness.
